newsitem.title: USA: Central & South West sees power sale dip.
newsitem.headline: Central & South West sees power sale dip.

text.p: Central and South West Corp expects a dip in power sales this year, but still expects demand to increase an average of 2.2 percent per year for the five year period 1996 through 2000, according to the utility's lastest financial forecast.
Its Financial Forecast - September 1996 projects a 1.4 percent decline in megawatt sales to 61.3 million this year.
It also sees a 2.5 percent increase next year, followed by increases of 2.0 percent, 2.2 percent and 2.2 percent in 1998, 1999 and 2000, respectively.

Central and South West is also projecting five-year construction spending of $2.71 billion, the company said, noting its projections for the period exclude any estimate for Transok, which was sold to Tejas Gas Corp in June.

This year's spending is now expected to total $481 million, up from $474 million in 1995. For the next four years, the company sees spending of $520 million, $509 million, $623 million and $575 million, the forecast said.
It projects a jump to total capital requirements this year to $2.08 billion from $838 million in 1995 due to the need to pay off $1.55 billion of long term debt.

The company received $690 million for Trnasok, $490 million of which was used to pay off one of the bridge loans used to acquire Seaboard Plc. In February it sold 13.5 million common shares for $26.375 per share and its Public Service of Oklahoma subsidiary filed a shelf registration for $75 million of notes.

Central and South West expects its capital requirements to drop to $724 million next year and $540 million in 1998. They are expected to rise again, to $868 million, in 1999 before easing to $733 million in 2000.
